findings.title: [P2] Redact provider error text before recording calibration failures
findings.body: The new calibration exit copies the provider-controlled exception text directly into `message_redacted` and the stderr error response. A context-limit response that echoes a credential or sensitive prompt fragment can therefore expose it in diagnostic output. Apply the existing redaction helper before recording or formatting the exception; the added `test_calibration_exit_redacts_secret_shapes_in_the_recorded_message` exercises this exact case.

findings.description: Numbers parsed out of a provider's HTTP 400/413 error body (`input_tokens`, `limit` via parse_context_limit) are written unvalidated into the persistent `.run/ceiling-observed.json` store and become the input bound for every later invocation of that (provider, model) until an operator recalibrates (test shows observed_for == limit+1 and the next 600K call preempts). There is no sanity check against the catalog entry (e.g. limit must be <= context_window and >= some floor), and when the message states no numbers the code records cheval's own estimate (`_obs = _walk_estimate`) as the observed failure point. Any 400 whose text happens to satisfy is_context_limit_message (a misclassified validation error, a proxy/gateway error page, a compromised or MITM'd endpoint) therefore permanently lowers the bound, and a body claiming `> 1 maximum` blocks the model entirely. The write is also reached from the non-walkable path, so a single bad response ends the call AND poisons future ones.
findings.failure_mode: A provider-side or intermediary-crafted error body persistently disables or shrinks a model's usable input window for all subsequent runs (self-inflicted DoS of the dispatch path) with no operator action other than a stderr hint.
findings.suggested_fix: Validate parsed values before recording: require provider_limit to be a positive int no greater than the entry's context_window and no smaller than FLOOR_MAX_TOKENS; ignore (do not record) observations that lack provider numbers instead of substituting the estimate; cap the number of lowering events per entry or require N consistent observations before the bound is lowered; log rejected observations.

findings.description: The provider's raw error text is stored as `models_failed[].message_redacted` via `str(_exc)` and echoed into the stderr `_error_json(...)` line without passing through the redaction helper, even though the field name promises redaction and the accompanying test (test_calibration_exit_redacts_secret_shapes_in_the_recorded_message) asserts that a secret-shaped fragment in the provider body never reaches the envelope or stderr. In that test the modelinv redaction is patched to identity, so the only place redaction can happen is here, and the diff does not do it. Provider 400 bodies can echo request fragments (system prompt excerpts, tool payloads) which may contain credentials.
findings.failure_mode: Secret-shaped strings echoed by a provider error body land in the MODELINV audit envelope and the operator log, where they are retained and may be shipped elsewhere.
findings.suggested_fix: Run both the recorded message and the `_error_json` message through the same redaction helper the rest of the walk loop uses (redact_payload_strings / assert_no_secret_shapes_remain) before appending to models_failed and printing; keep only the classified summary (status, class, numbers) in the stderr JSON.

findings.description: The long-context premium trigger compares only `input_tokens` against the threshold. Anthropic's usage splits prompt tokens into input_tokens, cache_read_input_tokens and cache_creation_input_tokens, and the published 1M-window premium applies when the total prompt (all three) exceeds 200K. A request with, e.g., 190K cached + 30K fresh input is billed at the base rate here while the provider bills the premium (input x2, output x1.5). Because the ledger feeds the daily-spend budget enforcer, exactly the most expensive requests are systematically under-counted, so the spend cap (a security control against runaway cost) under-fires.
findings.failure_mode: Budget enforcement and cost reports understate real spend on long-context requests by up to the multiplier, allowing spend to exceed the configured cap undetected.
findings.suggested_fix: Trigger on `input_tokens + cache_read_tokens + cache_creation_tokens > threshold` (and document the rule); add a test where cache tokens push the total over 200K.

findings.description: The allowlist regex ends in `$` and is applied with `re.match`. In Python `$` also matches before a trailing newline, so `"context-1m-2025-08-07\n"` passes validation and the newline is joined into the `anthropic-beta` header value. Both urllib and httpx reject CR/LF in header values, so the practical result is an unhandled ValueError on the request path (and a silent None from count_tokens) rather than header injection, but the stated guarantee ("anything outside the allowlist is a configuration error") is not actually enforced for this shape.
findings.failure_mode: A catalog value with a trailing newline (easy to introduce via YAML block scalars) passes the allowlist, then crashes dispatch with an untyped exception instead of a ConfigError naming the entry.
findings.suggested_fix: Use `_BETA_HEADER_RE.fullmatch(item)` or end the pattern with `\Z`; add a test with a trailing newline.

findings.description: `_mult` accepts any float with `m > 0`, including `inf` (a valid YAML scalar `.inf`). `int(inp_cost * inf)` raises OverflowError inside calculate_total_cost, which runs in the ledger path after the billed call, so the cost row is never written. Multipliers below 1.0 are also accepted and silently discount the premium tier.
findings.failure_mode: A malformed multiplier crashes post-call metering (lost ledger rows, budget counter not updated) instead of being rejected at config load.
findings.suggested_fix: Reject non-finite values (`math.isfinite`) and require multipliers >= 1.0 in _long_context_fields; surface the rejection as a ConfigError or warning rather than defaulting.

findings.description: The generated bash file interpolates the YAML model key directly into `["<key>"]="<n>"` without escaping. The value side is guarded by `select(type == "number")`, but a key containing `"`, `$(`, or backticks would break out of the string in the sourced generated-model-maps.sh and execute when flatline-orchestrator.sh sources it. The catalog is operator-controlled, so this is a hardening gap rather than an exploitable path, but the new array repeats the pattern instead of using `@sh` quoting.
findings.failure_mode: A crafted or accidentally malformed model key in model-config.yaml becomes shell code executed by every script that sources the generated map.
findings.suggested_fix: Emit keys with jq's `@sh` (or validate keys against `^[A-Za-z0-9._:-]+$` and fail generation otherwise), and apply the same to the sibling arrays.
